subject: Chemistry
solution:
The question text is cut off after "50"; it is assumed to read "on treatment with 50% KOH".
Molar ratio $\mathrm{C:O:H}=1:1:1$, so the empirical formula is $\mathrm{CHO}$ with empirical formula mass $12+1+16=29\ \mathrm{g\,mol^{-1}}$.
$n=\dfrac{58}{29}=2$, so the molecular formula is $\mathrm{C_2H_2O_2}$.
$\mathrm{C_2H_2O_2}$ is glyoxal, $\mathrm{OHC{-}CHO}$, which has no α-hydrogen.
Key concept: a dialdehyde with no α-H undergoes an intramolecular Cannizzaro reaction with 50% $\mathrm{KOH}$. One $\mathrm{{-}CHO}$ group is oxidised to $\mathrm{{-}COO^-}$ and the other is reduced to $\mathrm{{-}CH_2OH}$.
$$\mathrm{OHC{-}CHO \xrightarrow{50\%\ KOH} HOCH_2{-}COO^-K^+ \xrightarrow{H_3O^+} HOCH_2{-}COOH}$$
The product is glycolic acid, $\mathrm{HO{-}CH_2{-}COOH}$, which matches option (C).
Answer: (C) $\mathrm{HOCH_2{-}COOH}$ (glycolic acid)
